recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. The current source satisfies FHIR-34192; any future edit should be a new OO wording decision rather than further application of this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-34192 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification OO change request for R6 asking to add text at the bottom of Observation Boundaries and Relationships: Observation is for observations about people, groups, devices, locations, substances, and procedures rather than the record itself; detailed source information can use Provenance; and in-depth commentary or evaluation of the Observation record itself can use ArtifactAssessment.
initial_application: The issue was applied before this reconciliation. Source commit 9f0cbe865ba4b8303561b9bd4c92f0dd999e65d5 added the requested Provenance/ArtifactAssessment paragraph to source/observation/observation-introduction.xml, and PR HL7/fhir#3549 merged the work on 2025-07-29. The Jira comment on FHIR-34192 links PR 3549.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini confirms Observation is an active current-build resource and ArtifactAssessment is also an active target resource. OO minutes on 2024-09-10 record adding the proposed disposition for this Observation boundary wording, and OO Main minutes on 2025-03-13 record block-vote approval at 12-0-0. Later FHIR-52317 Observation boundary commits added DeviceAlert context and split/restored the ArtifactAssessment paragraph without reversing the FHIR-34192 guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was necessary. Current source/observation/observation-introduction.xml already contains the requested Boundaries and Relationships paragraph with links to Provenance and ArtifactAssessment, so this run published an empty audit commit on the combined branch.

related_jiras.note: The earlier CDS issue added ArtifactAssessment as a core resource, making it a valid target for the Observation boundary link. It was used as context only and was not decided here.
Later Observation boundary edits added DeviceAlert context and preserved/restored the ArtifactAssessment paragraph, confirming the seed guidance still stands.
